body.statement: Whenever every \(\rho\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) fails its terminal sIDP call, does the handle \(H_{\mathrm{lock}}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C,\Omega)\) produce a represented residual forest and a rational interior one- or two-mechanism observational-fiber tangent satisfying \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\), or another explicit positive rational construction with the same full selected observational law and the same positive terminal denominator but a different terminal numerator? Can such an object be streamed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations?
body.justification: This is the exact missing bridge from graphical failure to a reusable nonidentification certificate; neither ordinary hedge disagreement nor semantic nonidentifiability supplies the denominator lock automatically.
body.gap: Chen--Mooij's residual-forest converse is unconditional, while no checked conditional-PAG or selected-hedge result coordinates all reachable role states and an informative selected denominator.
body.consumer: A positive answer upgrades Branch-sCIDP from a sound formula search to a formula-or-checkable-failure decision procedure for selected-cohort PAG analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: The missing implication is from failure of the terminal sIDP call at every reachable role state to a represented residual forest carrying either a rational one- or two-mechanism tangent with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\ne0\), or an alternative explicit denominator-locked positive rational model pair, together with synthesis in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
obligation.obstruction: Unconditional sIDP failure can supply a terminal-joint obstruction, but it does not force two observationally equivalent models to have the same selected conditioning denominator. Algebraically, nonidentification of the joint does not imply that the numerator row lies outside the row span of the observational and denominator lock rows. No frozen result coordinates this rank-separation property across all reachable role states or all represented residual forests.
obligation.attempted: The residual-forest handle was reduced to the exact one-mechanism rank test, and the same reduction suggests enlarging to a two-mechanism tangent when the first test fails. The explicit informative selected bow shows that a connected conditioning coordinate can pass the lock, while ratio-cancellation examples show why failure of a particular terminal joint is insufficient. What remains unproved is the exhaustive graphical dichotomy asserting that every all-branches-fail COPAG yields a passing finite rational template; neither the one-mechanism test nor an unspecified two-mechanism enlargement proves that coverage.
obligation.partial_result:
For any supplied rational interior one-mechanism template, the exact condition
\[
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T)
\]
is necessary and sufficient for that template to yield a positive rational pair with identical full selected observational law, identical positive terminal denominator, and different terminal numerator; such a pair is compilable and verifiable in polynomial time in its explicit input and output lengths.  The informative three-observed-vertex construction supplies one represented terminal forest for which the locked pair exists even though the conditioning variable is connected and informative.  These results do not establish that every residual forest produced by universal branch failure admits such a one- or two-mechanism direction.
